newsitem.title: USA: Catalogs relying on Postal Service during UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Catalogs relying on Postal Service during UPS strike.

text.p: The nation's catalog retailers say they are taking orders from customers but have switched most shipping to the U.S. Postal Service because of the Teamsters strike against United Parcel Service.

In a survey of member companies by the Direct Marketing Association released late Thursday, 81 percent of the catalog companies said they were using the U.S. Postal Service's priority mail and parcel post to get packages delivered.

Prior to the UPS strike, which entered its 12th day Friday, more than half of the DMA member companies used UPS in conjunction with other shippers. Thirty-seven percent used UPS exclusively, while 10 percent did not rely on UPS at all.
DMA said Federal Express is being used by 46 percent. RPS and Airborne Express follow at 17 percent and 13 percent, respectively.

The trade organization that represents catalog retailers said consumer perception of delivery difficulties has resulted in a decrease in orders at more than half of the companies, although 39 percent reported no decrease in customer orders.
Two-thirds of the member catalog companies said the strike, if it continues beyond two weeks, will have a serious impact on earnings.

Meanwhile, the Postal Service said Friday it would continue Sunday deliveries in select areas. Nicholas Barranca, an official with the Postal Service, told NBC's "Today" show that the service had hired about 4,100 employees to handle the crush and most mail was being delivered on time.
